text.text_excerpt: Love the casual, communal vibes here! Great for large groups -- I'd recommend bringing a few friends with you so you can try more types of pizza! It seems like the flavors rotate, because there were different ones on my 2 visits. They have a fridge filled with different drinks/beers as well. Their pizzas are very light, so it felt healthier than your average pizza chain. You can come here for a quick appetizer and drink before dinner, or make this your full meal, since you get to choose how big/small you want your slices. They make a dozen or so different types of pizzas which are on display. You can choose whichever types you want, tell them how big you want the slices, pay at the counte...

I thought the food was great! Definitely Italian style pizza. Will say that the flow of the restaurant is a little backwards but I'm sure they will get it together once they understand that they will draw in a crowd. Will be back again because it's so good. Many different toppings - fave was onion and the all meats one. If you are confused, they make you take a number to order. Once your number is called, you step up and place your order. Order as much or little as desired. Then you'll pay and they will toss it in the over and hand you ANOTHER number once the pizza is hot . When there is a rush, you will get confused but it's just too many numbers

It's great, but don't go expecting your everyday pizza parlor. It's more like a deli and a bakery had a pizza-baby and that pizza-baby grew up and moved to New Orleans. It's a polished concept restaurant that looks like it's supposed to be a quick lunch spot for busy people. You'd think it'd be quick - they just cut the pizza right in front of you. I kinda figured they'd hand it to me right there. Instead, we had to grab a seat and they brought it to us. It's not like it took very long, but at the same time, not sure why it took any time at all (there's probably a good reason, I just don't know what it is). The pizza itself was great.
